[EFFECT]
Wind speed has a mostly negative effect on hourly bike demand — the faster the wind, the fewer bikes the model predicts will be rented. At very low wind speeds (roughly under 8 km/h), the contribution is essentially neutral or a tiny touch positive. From about 20 km/h upward, the contribution drops steadily and sharply, reaching its most negative value at the highest wind speeds observed (~50–55 km/h), where predicted demand is reduced by roughly 30% compared to calm conditions. The peak contribution therefore occurs at the calmest hours, and the effect worsens progressively as wind picks up.

[IMPORTANCE]
Windspeed is the **second-least important** feature in the model, ranked **8th out of 9**, with an importance score of 0.014 — far below the dominant features like hour of day (0.89), temperature (0.25), and year (0.22). Its influence is real but modest compared to those top drivers.

[RECOMMENDATION]
On forecasted high-wind days (above roughly 20 km/h), planners can expect noticeably lower rental demand, so bike rebalancing needs and staffing levels can be trimmed slightly; conversely, calm and still days are unlikely to need a wind-related adjustment as the effect there is negligible.
